node.label: IT Rules & content takedowns
node.summary: IT Act blocking powers, intermediary rules, safe harbour and takedowns.

facts.text: Users whose posts are removed under a platform's own rules must go to its **grievance officer**, then the government's **Grievance Appellate Committee** (30 days). In **Shreya Singhal v Union of India (2015)** the SC struck down **Section 66A** but upheld 69A.

facts.text: Takedown law: **Section 69A** of the **IT Act, 2000** lets the Centre block content on grounds like sovereignty, security and public order; **Section 79** gives platforms **safe harbour**, lost under **79(3)(b)** if they fail to act on notice. MeitY advisories of **8 and 10 Oct** (the second to **Meta**) preceded a wave of takedowns amid anti-CEC protests.

facts.text: **IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026**: under Rule **3(1)(d)**, platforms must take down unlawful content within **3 hours** (down from **36 hours**) of a court order or a reasoned government intimation; synthetic (AI) content must be labelled.
